name: Clindamycin
summary: Lincosamide with potent anaerobic coverage and exotoxin suppression; useful for aspiration, dental, and skin infections.
mechanism: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis (overlaps the macrolide binding site).
pharmacodynamics: Time-dependent killing with a prolonged post-antibiotic effect.

dosing.adult: PO: 150-450 mg every 6-8 hours; IV: 600-900 mg every 8 hours

safety.lactation: Compatible — monitor infant for GI effects
warnings: C. difficile colitis — among the highest-risk antibiotics
Poor CNS penetration — do not use for meningitis

indications: Skin and soft-tissue infections (incl. some MRSA)
Adjunct in streptococcal toxic shock syndrome / necrotizing fasciitis (toxin suppression)
clinicalPearls: Suppresses exotoxin synthesis — valuable adjunct in invasive group A strep disease
C. difficile risk is high — avoid unless clearly indicated
good: Potent anaerobic coverage plus toxin suppression in invasive strep disease.
bad: C. difficile risk, poor CNS penetration, and no Gram-negative activity.
